content.hemodynamic_definition: Mean pulmonary artery pressure ≥25 mmHg along with pulmonary arterial wedge pressure ≤15 mmHg, documented at right heart catheterization in a patient with mismatched perfusion defects on V/Q lung scan.
content.specific_angiographic_signs: On multidetector CT angiography or conventional pulmonary cineangiography: ring-like stenoses, webs, slits, and chronic total occlusions are specific diagnostic signs for CTEPH.
content.CTED_note: Some patients may present with normal pulmonary haemodynamics at rest despite symptomatic disease; if other causes of exercise limitation are excluded these patients are considered to have chronic thromboembolic disease (CTED). Among 1,019 patients submitted to pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) in a UK centre, 42 patients did not have pulmonary hypertension at rest but showed functional improvement after the operation.
content.planar_VQ_performance: Planar V/Q lung scan recommended as first-line imaging for CTEPH: reported sensitivity approximately 96–97% and specificity approximately 90–95% for diagnosis. SPECT appears less sensitive than planar V/Q when assessed at the level of individual segmental arteries but is unlikely to miss clinically relevant CTEPH in an individual patient.
content.CTPA_and_other_imaging: CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is increasingly used but should not be a standalone test to exclude disease. Newer tests include dual-energy CT for simultaneous assessment of pulmonary artery patency and lung perfusion. MRI of the pulmonary vasculature is still considered inferior to CT. Cone-beam CT, angioscopy, intravascular ultrasound, and optical coherence tomography are more suitable for lesion characterization during interventional treatment. High-resolution chest CT may assist differential diagnosis and show emphysema, bronchial or interstitial lung disease, infarcts, and vascular/thoracic wall malformations.
content.perfusion_patterns: Perfusion inequalities manifesting as a mosaic parenchymal pattern are frequently found in CTEPH but may also be observed in about 12% of patients with other causes of pulmonary hypertension.
content.differential_diagnosis: Differential diagnosis of CTEPH should include pulmonary arteritis, pulmonary angiosarcoma, tumour embolism, parasites (hydatid cyst), foreign body embolism, and congenital or acquired pulmonary artery stenoses.
content.surgical_treatment_overview: Surgical pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) is the treatment of choice for operable CTEPH. Unlike acute pulmonary embolus embolectomy, CTEPH requires a true bilateral endarterectomy through the medial layer of the pulmonary arteries, with deep hypothermia and intermittent circulatory arrest, without a need for cerebral perfusion.
content.surgical_outcomes: In-hospital mortality reported as low as 4.7% and lower in high-volume single centres. The majority of patients experience substantial symptom relief and near-normalization of haemodynamics after PEA.
